fields.v: Shafin, W. I., Rafi, M. N., Li, Z., Chen, T.-H. (2025). Evaluating Software Process Models for Multi-Agent Class-Level Code Generation. arXiv:2511.09794v1 [cs.SE], 12 Nov 2025
Preprint — arXiv:2511.09794v1 [cs.SE], 12 Nov 2025; ACM template placeholders ('Conference acronym XX', 2018), no venue stated
SPEAR Lab, Concordia University, Montreal, Canada (Shafin, Rafi, Chen); York University, Toronto, Canada (Li)

Compares — ablation study of a Waterfall-style multi-agent LLM workflow (Requirement, Design, Implementation, Testing; full and without Requirement, Design or Testing) against direct prompting (RawPrompt) with three LLMs on 100 ClassEval tasks: Pass@1, SonarQube quality, runtime error types and a manual root-cause taxonomy
fields.why: The Waterfall multi-agent workflow is the authors' class-level adaptation of SOEN-101 (which seems to come from the same lab), and Q12 already treats them as its vendor (Partly). The paper frames itself as an evaluation ('first systematic study'), so 'Compares' holds, but a reader could file it as 'Proposes an approach; secondary: Compares', which would make Q13 applicable.
fields.doubt: O workflow Waterfall é uma adaptação dos próprios autores (do SOEN-101), mas o artigo apresenta-se como estudo de avaliação. Decide se fica Compares ou Proposes an approach; neste caso a Q13 passa a aplicar-se.

fields.v: Waterfall-inspired multi-agent workflow (authors' class-level adaptation of the SOEN-101 prompt structure), four agent roles: Requirement Engineer, Architect, Developer, Tester; variants Full, w/o-Requirement, w/o-Design, w/o-Testing; baseline RawPrompt. Models: gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18, deepseek-chat (DeepSeek-V3-0324), claude-3-5-haiku-20241022; temperature 0.8. No coding-agent tool (custom pipeline); no version of the workflow

Quality verdict for each: no criterion stated by the authors. Cost verdict: not measured

Tasks: 100 ClassEval tasks. Configurations: 3 models × (RawPrompt + 4 Waterfall variants). Baseline: RawPrompt (direct generation from the task description). Held constant: tasks, role prompt template, temperature 0.8, holistic class generation, evaluation framework. Acceptance tests: ClassEval unit tests. Repetitions: one sample per task (Pass@1). Human intervention: manual fixing of simple syntax errors before re-running (error analysis)

Class-level Pass@1 falls under Waterfall for gpt-4o-mini (0.35 → 0.21-0.23, -34% to -40%) and deepseek-chat (0.46 → 0.19-0.32, -30% to -59%) and rises for claude-3.5-haiku (0.21 → 0.22-0.29) except w/o-Testing (0.17); function-level for claude +18% to +70%. Maintainability issues lower for gpt-4o-mini (-3% to -19%), mixed for the others; Consistency issues lower for all (-5% to -43%); Adaptability issues higher for gpt-4o-mini (+191% to +391%) and deepseek-chat (+13% to +95%), mixed for claude. Runtime errors +10% to +53%; most errors with w/o-Testing for deepseek-chat (124) and claude-3.5-haiku (111), with Full for gpt-4o-mini (122 vs 118 for w/o-Testing). Missing Code falls; Semantic Failure, Return Mismatch and Input Validation rise; Dataset issues most common (47-62). No significance tests

Ablation distinguished phase effects (Testing strongest, Requirement and Design modest) and model-dependent effects. Not repeated: one sample at temperature 0.8, variability not estimated. Limitations stated: Pass@1 volatile; qualitative root-cause analysis subjective; Waterfall only approximated by LLM roles; LLM-generated tests

Threats: subjective manual root-cause analysis and possible categorisation inconsistencies; Pass@1 single-attempt and volatile; approximation of the real Waterfall process and phase combinations; LLM-generated test suites. Gaps / future work: adaptive pipelines that enable or skip stages, cross-stage memory and reconciliation, conflict-resolution meta-agent preferring the benchmark contract; benchmarks with explicit contract policies, dual scores (correctness and design quality), spec-faithfulness checks, ambiguity labels; LLM-based evaluators; Pynguin or hybrid test generation

Inconsistencies: abstract figures (-37.8%, -39.8%, +9.5%) are not in Table 2; they equal the averages of the four Waterfall variants' class-level changes (pp. 1, 6). Text says w/o-Test 'consistently leads to the highest failure rates across all models' and also that 'the full Waterfall process leads to the highest number of runtime errors' (p. 8); Table 3 gives gpt-4o-mini Full 122 vs w/o-Test 118, deepseek-chat 96 vs 124, claude 99 vs 111. Text says deepseek-chat Missing Code fell 'from 10 to just a single case' (p. 9) while Table 5 gives 1 for RawPrompt (p. 10). RQ2 says all 1,500 samples were evaluated manually (p. 7), the threats section says outputs were 'randomly sampled' (p. 10). Text says reliability worsens in all Waterfall settings (p. 6), but Table 2 has zero reliability issues in some variant cells. Table 2 Reliability column and Table 5 Waterfall columns jumbled in the extracted text. Code and data: anonymous repository (anonymous.4open.science/r/LLMCLWA-3XB). Pre-registration: not claimed.
